newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - products creep higher.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - products creep higher.

text.p: Prices of Gulf refined oil products were seen slowly creeping higher in the week to Thursday, traders based in the Middle East Gulf said.
"Middle distillates seem to be getting back towards balance, particularly on gas oil," one said, adding he had heard deals were being concluded at premiums of around 50 cents.
Another concurred: "In one percent gas oil there have been a few deals at 50 cents (premium)."
A week earlier, the premium on one percent gas oil was seen no better than 40 cents a barrel, down 10-20 cents on the week and nearly a dollar lower than October highs.
"The market has been oscillating. It has a bearing on the IOC (Indian Oil Corp) awards. The latest one was only a small volume," a trader said.
India bought in a tender a modest 255,000 tonnes of diesel for delivery in January, down from initial expectations of 700,000 tonnes.
The previous IOC tender for December delivery had been for 520,000 tonnes of diesel in 13 cargoes. Traders had been expecting at least similar purchasing levels for January.
One trader saw the premium for 0.5 percent gas oil in December up at 75 to 80 cents. He said jet premiums were also moving higher -- to around 65 and 70 cents from 40 cents.
"No deals have been done recently in kerosene, but we are noticing that it is going up, with requirements in Japan, Korea and Indonesia," he said
Gas oil was assessed at $29.80/$30.00 a barrel fob Gulf on Thursday and jet was at $31.60/90.

After gaining $6 in two days last week, the Fujairah bunker market was subdued this week. 380-cst bunker fuel from the Gulf port was assessed on Thursday at $116 a tonne and 180-cst was at $122 from $126-128 last week.
